text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.24% today to close at $126.75, marking the fourth down day in five trading sessions. The immediate pressure came from the G7's announcement that it will release 100 million barrels of diesel reserves over the next four months—a direct supply intervention designed to cool fuel prices amid regional conflicts. When governments flood markets with reserves, it typically weighs on crude prices and the profits oil majors can generate, which is why the stock has declined 3.85% over the past two weeks as this supply relief effort has become concrete.

The broader backdrop remains volatile and mixed for oil producers. Geopolitical tensions—including potential U.S. strikes on Iran and supply disruptions from Middle East conflicts—are supporting crude prices at higher levels (Brent at $113.96/barrel), but government intervention to release reserves and India's risk of tariffs for buying Russian oil are countervailing headwinds. The company is caught between structural support from regional instability and policy-driven pressure to cool energy markets.
